source: Real paper AuDHD_2.pdf (Data-17072026/, 3,966,494 bytes). A deterministic corrupted variant was created by truncating the raw file bytes to exactly the first 60% of the original byte length (int(len(raw) * 0.60) = 2,379,896 bytes), written to a temp file and deleted after the run -- reproducible by re-running this script (evals/benchmarks/v3/seed_from_real_corpus.py), which regenerates the identical truncated byte sequence from the same source PDF.
description: Exercises the corrupted/truncated-PDF path through both real parsers used by pipeline/extraction_reconciler.py's multi-parser reconciliation: pipeline.pdf_parser.parse_pdf() (pdfplumber/pdfminer) and pipeline.docling_parser.extract_with_docling() (Docling/pdfium). Captures what ACTUALLY happens against a real corrupted PDF, not an assumed graceful-degradation contract.

observed_behavior.finding: BOTH real parsers raise a hard, uncaught-at-their-level exception on this 60%-truncated PDF -- neither returns a degraded-but-non-crashing result (no partial char_count, no partial sections/tables). pdf_parser.parse_pdf() raises pdfplumber.utils.exceptions.PdfminerException wrapping a pdfminer PDFNoValidXRef/PSEOF ('Unexpected EOF'); docling_parser.extract_with_docling() raises docling.exceptions.ConversionError wrapping a pypdfium2 PdfiumError ('Data format error'). Checked directly against app.py's real call sites (2026-08-24): parse_pdf() is called at Stage 1 (app.py ~line 1185) with NO local try/except of its own -- only the single outer `except Exception as e:` around the entire multi-stage run (app.py ~line 1646, `st.error(f'Pipeline error: {e}')`) catches it, meaning one corrupted PDF anywhere in a multi-paper upload batch aborts the ENTIRE run for every paper, with nothing saved. extract_with_docling(), by contrast, IS wrapped in a real per-paper try/except at Stage 2B (app.py ~lines 1290-1302): a Docling failure there degrades only that paper's `reconciled` to `{'fields': {}}` (lowering its completeness score) without aborting the run. So 'the multi-parser reconciliation's graceful-degradation path' genuinely exists, but only on the Docling side -- the primary pdf_parser.parse_pdf() path that runs first has no equivalent per-paper recovery today, which is a real, narrow gap for a future story.
